introduction_markdown: Answer BOTH sections in the SAME answer booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Begin with SECTION A. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. In the Directed Writing question avoid indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer because this will earn you no marks. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you no marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Time allowed: two hours.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity (e.g. your name, school, parentage etc). You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **c)** Your relative or friend who lives in the village has dropped out of school. Write a letter to him/her bringing out the importance of education to one's life and convincing him/her to go back to school. Your name is Dada Vita, P.O Box 1146 Dimba and your relative's or friend's name is Emblem Dibo.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Sender's address and date (top right), salutation "Dear Emblem,".
2. Opening: greetings and the reason for writing.
3. Understand his/her reasons, then show the limits of quick money from the farm.
4. Importance of education: a career, thinking skills, respect, help for the family.
5. Encouragement and practical help, then an informal ending with the name Dada Vita.

**Model composition (464 words)**

P.O Box 1146
Dimba
15th June 2023

Dear Emblem,

I hope this letter finds you in good health and good spirits. I am well, and so is everyone at home, thank God. I was very sad to learn from your sister that you have left school. I could not sleep that night, because I know how intelligent you are. I am writing, therefore, not to scold you, but to speak to you as a friend who wants the very best for you, and to beg you to go back to school.

I understand that life in the village is not easy. Perhaps school fees were difficult to pay, or perhaps you felt that the farm and a small business could give you quick money. I understand these worries. But think carefully about what you are giving up. Money from the farm may come quickly, but it is small and uncertain. An education opens doors that no farm can open. With a certificate you can become a teacher, a nurse, an engineer, a lawyer or a skilled technician. You will earn a decent salary, and you will also help your parents and younger brothers and sisters in the future.

Education does much more than prepare one for a job. It teaches us how to think, to reason and to solve problems. An educated person can read a contract before signing it, understand a doctor's advice, and use modern methods to make a farm more productive. Nobody can easily cheat such a person. Education also gives us confidence and respect in society. Do you remember how the whole village listened to Mr. Tanyi when he returned as a doctor? That respect came from his years of study.

I also want you to remember that you are still young. At your age, it is not too late to return. Many pupils have left school for a year or two and later come back and succeeded. If the problem is money, you can ask the headmaster about a payment plan or a scholarship, and I will gladly share my old textbooks with you. If the problem is difficulty in a particular subject, we can study together during the holidays when I come to the village. I promise to help you in mathematics, which I know was giving you trouble.

Please do not let the difficulties of today destroy the dreams of tomorrow. Talk to your parents and let them know that you wish to return. I am sure they will be happy and will support you in every way they can. Write to me as soon as you have decided, and I will be waiting eagerly for your reply.

Give my warm greetings to your parents and to all our friends in the village.

Yours lovingly,
Dada Vita

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Wrong letter format: no address, no date, no salutation or ending, or writing as a formal letter to an official.
2. Scolding the friend instead of persuading, or ignoring the imposed names and address (Dada Vita, P.O Box 1146 Dimba, Emblem Dibo).
